fieldMarks: Medium non-venomous snake, 75-130 cm typical (up to 178 cm), with smooth glossy scales.
Light beige or grey ground colour with dark-edged blotches filled with gold, brown or olive-grey.
Prominent eye stripe, lidless eyes with slightly vertical pupils, single anal scale, countersunk lower jaw.
Juveniles similar but darker marked, lightening with age; sexes alike.
behavior: Crepuscular and nocturnal, mostly active April-September; primarily nocturnal, sometimes by day.
Excellent burrower; uses crevices and rodent burrows as daytime retreats. Constrictor; about half its diet is other reptiles, especially lizards.
Gentle and calm; moves by lateral undulation.
habitat: Semi-arid grassland, sandy desert and scrub, sagebrush flats, chaparral and rocky washes, preferring open areas with sandy or loamy soil.
Shelters and lays eggs underground; from below sea level to about 2,200 m.
range: Central and southern California, southern Nevada, southern Utah, Colorado, southern Nebraska, Kansas, Oklahoma, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas, south into Baja California and Mexico; not in Canada.
